# medrev

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

`medrev` turns a research question into a folder of open-access PDFs plus the
audit tables a literature review needs. It searches the literature through
[Europe PubMed Central](https://europepmc.org/RestfulWebService) (which indexes
all of PubMed and MEDLINE), de-duplicates, tracks screening decisions, resolves
open-access full text, and downloads it. Record tables are
[`basetable`](https://github.com/ielbadisy/basetable) objects. Only open-access
content is fetched; closed-access hits are reported, never scraped.

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("ielbadisy/medrev")
```

## Usage

```r
library(medrev)

r <- pubmed("machine learning for sepsis prediction", n = 300, years = c(2018, 2025))
r <- dedup(r, fuzzy = TRUE)
r <- screen(r, exclude = year < 2019, reason = "pre-2019 protocol")

fetch(r, dir = "sepsis_pdfs", name = "{year}_{pmid}")   # resolves OA links + downloads
prisma(r)                                               # PRISMA-style flow counts
bibliography(r, "sepsis.ris")                           # RIS / BibTeX / CSV by extension
```

Start from a reference list instead of a query:

```r
r <- pubmed(ids = c("31452104", "10.1038/s41586-020-2649-2"))
```

Hand-screening in a spreadsheet:

```r
sheet <- screen(r)                 # editable: fill the `decision` column
# ... edit sheet ...
r <- screen(r, sheet = sheet)
```

## Configuration

Unpaywall (one of the PDF resolvers) needs a contact e-mail:

```r
options(medrev.email = "you@example.org")   # or set MEDREV_EMAIL
```

## The `medrev` object

A single carrier: `$records` (the record table), `$searches` (query log), and
`$stages` (row count after each step, which drives `prisma()`).
`as.data.frame(r)` returns the record table.
